title: Dynamic Reserve Guardrails for Dedicated Capacity (soft reserves, tenant burst windows, and prewarm tokens)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Customers with Dedicated pools need predictable throughput for critical tenants while we also allow short-duration bursts to absorb traffic spikes. Current reserved pool primitives are static and either over-provision (high cost) or under-provision (SLO violations). This PRD defines a set of dynamic reserve guardrails: soft reserves that can be temporarily augmented by burst windows, tenant-scoped prewarm tokens for rapid scale-up, and safe soft-eviction thresholds with graceful degradation fallbacks.
requirements: Soft reserve objects: define initial reservation and a dynamic headroom range (percentage) that can be used for bursts
Burst windows: per-tenant configurable short-duration burst allowance (tokens or vCPU/GPU units) with cooldowns
Prewarm tokens: small reusable token buckets per-tenant that enable instant KV-cache and model prewarm on first request after idle
Soft-eviction policy: prioritized, observable soft-evict decisions when capacity hits critical utilization with automatic fallback to permissible model variants
Cost controller: telemetry hooks exposing per-tenant effective cost impact and cumulative burst consumption for billing/reporting
Safety rails: global caps and tenant-level limits, and automatic rollback path for misconfiguration
API/Console UX: expose reserve, burst, and prewarm settings in Console + SDK with validation and recommended defaults
Metrics and alerts: new SLO metrics (burst_saturation_rate, prewarm_hit_rate, soft_eviction_count), and runbook templates for ops
scope: In scope: design and implement soft reserve semantics in Dedicated control plane, API and Console controls for configuring burst windows and prewarm tokens, autoscaling interaction rules, and SLO/observability changes. Out-of-scope: billing product changes for metered burst billing (billing team follow-up), private on-prem installer packaging for this feature (handled separately).
out_of_scope: On-prem packaging and air-gapped installer changes
acceptance_criteria: Create 'soft_reserve' API that accepts initial_units, burst_headroom_pct, and cooldown_seconds; returns 200 and a stable ID
Console surfaces an editable soft reserve UI with recommended defaults and client-side validation

When pool utilization exceeds initial_units but is within initial_units + headroom, requests are allowed and burst consumption is recorded; when beyond headroom, requests are throttled or routed to fallback model according to policy
Prewarm tokens permit sub-100ms cold-start latency for first token-prefetch request in 90% of test scenarios (p95 < 100ms) for targeted models
Soft-eviction events are logged with tenant_id, reason, and decision path; on soft-evict, a fallback model is used and request latency degradation is <2x baseline for 95% calls
Dashboard shows per-tenant burst usage and a cost estimate; alerts fire when any tenant consumes >75% of configured burst allowance in a 1-hour window
Integration tests cover autoscaler interplay with soft reserves (3 scenarios: normal load, burst ramp, sustained overload) and corresponding rollbacks/pass criteria
rollout_plan: Phase 1: API + backend implementation behind feature flag for internal clusters (2 weeks). Phase 2: Console UX + experimental enable per-customer with opt-in (2 weeks). Phase 3: Gradual ramp to wider customers with telemetry review and a canary guard at 10% of dedicated pools (2 weeks). Final: GA release and docs (1 week).
testing_plan: Unit tests for API validation and calculations; end-to-end integration tests in staging that simulate tenant traffic patterns (normal, spike, sustained overload); chaos test to force node failures and observe soft-eviction behavior; manual QA for Console flows and permission gating.

open_questions: Should burst consumption be billable instantly or invoiced as part of monthly reconciliation?
What should be the global default headroom_pct to balance cost vs reliability?
How do we reconcile prewarm tokens across model variants that share the same KV cache?
decisions: Prefer soft reserves with an explicit headroom percentage vs pure token-only burst model (2026-03-04)
Require security review prior to GA due to tenant isolation and telemetry exposure (2026-03-06)
